html:
SMTO-GML-0025 — Gmail kept sending the same page of search results

GUID: cbbe38b2-a1ab-4dc6-af78-b700d9bed6f6
Slug: gmail-provider-pagination-invalid
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO was going through your Gmail search results page by page, but Gmail kept sending a page it had already sent. SMTO stopped to avoid going in circles. No emails were changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to run the same search or count again from the beginning. A fresh search asks Gmail for every page again from the start, which may get past the repeated page.
  2. If it happens again, narrow the search, for example add a date range, a sender or a label. Fewer results means fewer pages, which avoids the page that repeated.
  3. For a change to many emails, ask SMTO for a new preview after the search succeeds, and check it before approving. The earlier search didn't finish, so its list of emails can't be used.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the number of matching emails or a preview without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the search you asked for, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't approve a bulk change based on the incomplete search.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail message selection stopped because the provider's messages.list returned a nextPageToken that had already been seen in the same enumeration, which would otherwise loop forever.

What this means

  • Mailbox selection encounters a nextPageToken already seen during the same provider enumeration. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Mailbox selection encounters a nextPageToken already seen during the same provider enumeration.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the retained page sequence and original query without assuming enumeration is complete.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._select_ids (used by gmail.count and gmail.preview_modify) tracks nextPageToken values and raises gmail_provider_pagination_invalid on a repeat. Re-run the count or preview from the first page; if it recurs, narrow the query (date range, sender, label) and capture the query, account_ref and Server log for a provider-side pagination defect.
  • Restart the search from its first page and inspect provider pagination diagnostics if it repeats.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • A bounded fresh supported read advances consistently or reports the provider pagination defect.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
